justification: Removes credential literals from 17 tracked files. The gate is right to refuse 'minor' here: 15 substantive files change, and the edit alters how every one of them obtains a credential at runtime. No logic, control flow, database or served output changes, but the failure mode moves from 'works with a smuggled key' to 'fails without a configured one', which is a real behaviour change across a wide surface.

break_it.scenario: Someone runs one of these scripts with no OPENAI_API_KEY in the environment and no repo .env.
break_it.what_happens: It now fails instead of working. That is the intended change: it previously 'worked' only because a live credential was inlined in the file. os.environ.get returns None and the OpenAI client raises on construction, naming the missing key. The alternative — a silent fallback — is what put the key in 16 files in the first place.
break_it.how: This matches the convention already in the codebase: scripts/openai_semantic_processor.py:15 is the identical os.environ.get form, and scripts/sol_common.py:load_api_key resolves env then repo .env/.env.local and raises a message naming exactly what to set. Anyone with a working .env is unaffected.

break_it.scenario: secondary_dwelling_stats.py loses its Supabase anon-key default and a scheduled job depends on that default.
break_it.what_happens: DA_SUPABASE_KEY becomes an empty string unless DA_SUPABASE_ANON_KEY is set, so the Supabase call is unauthenticated and fails. Callers are scripts/json_to_ts_stats.py and scripts/refresh_stats_job.py, so a stats refresh could break until the variable is set.
break_it.how: Not mitigated, and called out rather than hidden. The line was already os.environ.get("DA_SUPABASE_ANON_KEY", <literal>) so the environment was always preferred; only the inline fallback is gone. This key is the lowest-risk of the four — Supabase anon keys are designed to be shipped to browsers and are guarded by RLS — but it should still not sit in a tracked file. Set DA_SUPABASE_ANON_KEY wherever refresh_stats_job runs.

break_it.scenario: This PR is mistaken for having fixed the credential exposure.
break_it.what_happens: The keys stay valid and remain in git history on every prior commit, so anyone with the repo, a fork, or a stale clone still has working credentials. Removing them from the tip changes nothing about that.
break_it.how: Stated in the PR body and in ~/.claude/plans/meta-session-reconciliation-2026-08-11.md: ROTATION is the fix, this PR only stops the bleeding forward. A history rewrite is deliberately not attempted here — it would rewrite every SHA and break all 13 open PRs, and after rotation it is cosmetic.

post_merge.db_reset: No. No schema or data change. One Supabase anon-key default is removed; set DA_SUPABASE_ANON_KEY where refresh_stats_job runs.
post_merge.secrets: This IS the secrets change. Four distinct credentials removed from 17 tracked files. They remain valid and remain in history until rotated — rotation is a separate, required action.
post_merge.manual_verify: Yes, and it is the point: rotate the OpenAI, Anthropic and TfNSW keys. Then confirm any job that used the Supabase anon-key default has DA_SUPABASE_ANON_KEY set.

falsifiable_check.fails_when: It prints anything other than 0. Measured: 16 at origin/main, 0 at this branch's HEAD. 16 rather than 17 because this command matches the two sk- key families; the 17th file holds the Supabase anon JWT, which is checked by the same sweep in the PR body but is deliberately not in this pattern because a JWT regex also matches ordinary base64. The check is falsifiable in both directions and is not self-referential: it SEARCHES the tracked tree with git rather than diffing the change that produced it, so a literal I failed to notice still fails it, and re-introducing any sk- key makes it non-zero.
falsifiable_check.external_authority: The pattern set comes from the vendors' own key formats (sk-ant-api03, sk-proj, JWT), not from anything this change defines, and git ls-files decides what is tracked. Rotation was confirmed independently by hashing the .env values against the values published in the repo: the Anthropic key matched before rotation and does not match after.

pre_impl.existing_data: Audited before editing: 4 distinct secrets across 17 tracked files, not the 3 files first reported. One OpenAI key appears in 15 scripts and 2 docs; an Anthropic key in 2 docs; a TfNSW JWT in 1 doc; a Supabase anon key in 1 script. Counted by hashing every match over git ls-files rather than by eyeballing grep output.
pre_impl.assumption_mismatch: I expected these to be dead experiment scripts that could simply be deleted. They are not: lightrag-hku==1.5.4 is still a declared dependency in requirements.txt, src/processing/__init__.py imports real_lightrag_processor, and refresh_stats_job.py calls secondary_dwelling_stats. So deletion was wrong and substitution was the only safe option.
pre_impl.external_source_error: No network call is made. The replacement resolves from os.environ, and the repo's own resolver (scripts/sol_common.py:load_api_key) additionally falls back to .env/.env.local and raises a message naming the variable. A missing key now fails loudly at the point of use instead of silently succeeding with an inlined credential.
pre_impl.new_vs_existing: No new pattern is introduced. os.environ.get("OPENAI_API_KEY") is the form already used at scripts/openai_semantic_processor.py:15, so this makes 15 outliers match the existing convention.
